claims.text: The baseline catalyst is a nanoscale ordered intermetallic containing both platinum-group and secondary non-PGM metals.
The baseline catalyst can be represented by Pt–Pd intermetallic nanoparticles.
The baseline nanoscale catalyst has high ethanol-oxidation activity.
The baseline catalyst is selective for complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation.
The baseline catalyst has excellent long-term durability.
Incorporation of the secondary non-PGM metal creates adjacent active sites with a tuned d-band center.
The tuned d-band center optimizes the adsorption energies of CO and acetaldehyde intermediates.
Optimized intermediate adsorption promotes complete 12-electron and 12-proton ethanol oxidation.
The electronic modification minimizes surface poisoning.
The multi-element composition and associated electronic modification enhance catalyst durability.
The proposed controlled intervention is to reduce the secondary non-PGM fraction while holding morphology and particle size constant.
Changing the PGM-to-secondary-metal ratio shifts the d-band center.
The ordered intermetallic structure mediates optimal binding of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Optimal performance occurs when intermediates bind neither strongly enough to poison sites nor weakly enough to impede activation.
Balanced adsorption and desorption facilitate efficient electron transfer and full ethanol oxidation.
Reducing the secondary-metal fraction will produce a measurable d-band-center shift.
Reducing the secondary-metal fraction will lower ethanol-oxidation current density.
Reducing the secondary-metal fraction will decrease selectivity for the 12-electron pathway.
Reducing the secondary-metal fraction will reduce long-term cycling durability.
The proposed mechanism applies in alkaline ethanol oxidation but may cease to govern performance in acidic media or at substantially different potentials.

contradictions.description: The initial material is exemplified as Pt–Pd, which contains no non-PGM metal, whereas the intervention and baseline require an existing secondary non-PGM component whose fraction and PGM-to-secondary-metal ratio can be varied.
